objective: Proof: the fewest-knot presentations of a line of n distinctions are its bracketings (the literature's polygon triangulations); under KF3 the first new distinction fills one knot uniformly, and the chance of two orders after the second is an explicit sum over the knots' nesting read without order (which knot lies within which, from the knot holding both ends).
status: Proved 2026-11-18 (referee pending): the fewest-knot presentations of a line are exactly its bracketings; under KF3 the first new distinction fills a uniform knot, fills of triples keep two orders exactly when no middle lies strictly between another fill's ends except its own middle, and the second step's options are the other knots' fills and two re-bracketing fills per knot sharing a pair (finite check on all 6,916 bracketings to n0 = 11); so P(two orders after the second new distinction) = (1/(n-2)) sum [s + 2p + c]/[(n-3) + 2(p+c)], a function of the bare bracketing: 5/12 chains, 11/18 middle, 51/140 both six-starts.
title: How the knots nest decides the second fill
